extracted.intended_audience: researchers and nonprofit grant applicants (grant writers, PIs, program staff) preparing funding proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on common errors to avoid when developing and submitting grant proposals, plus a pre-submission checklist to improve compliance, clarity, and funder fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Following Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations, corporations, and government agencies sort applicants by whether they followed directions; failing to follow instructions is a top mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Read all instructions in the application package; use a checklist to double-check formatting, word count, and attachments; print out the RFA/NOFO and highlight requirements; have someone else verify compliance before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor Formatting and Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing basic formatting/margins/font/figure rules can lead to rejection even when content is good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Verify font (typically Arial, Helvetica, Palatino, Georgia, 11pt minimum); verify margins (0.5" minimum); use clear section headers; number figures and tables consistently; verify page limits before final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak or Vague Needs Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Not clearly articulating the problem the project addresses undermines funder understanding and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Use current data, case studies, and expert opinions; establish the problem clearly; show the issue's impact on targeted communities; use specific statistics, not generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misaligned Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets should reflect project priorities and narrative; inflated or unexplained budgets damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Make sure the budget aligns with the goals and timeline specified in the proposal; don't use round numbers or unsubstantiated cost estimates; justify each line item; match personnel effort to scope; avoid unjustified equipment requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing or Weak Evaluation Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Not showing how success will be measured is a critical oversight for funders who want measurable impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Include both process and outcome metrics; identify who will conduct the evaluation; specify data collection methods; include baseline assessments where appropriate; tie evaluation to specific objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Last-minute submissions often contain errors, missing forms, or lost attachments and look rushed to reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Plan for submission 1 week before deadline; account for institutional sign-off time (often 5+ business days); test all upload systems early; have backup plans for technical failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careless Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Typos and grammatical errors force reviewers to reread and reduce perceived professionalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Multiple proofreading passes; read aloud; use Grammarly or similar tools; have non-author proofread; don't rely solely on spell-check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Having a Compelling Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Project lacks a story arc; the reader can't follow why → what → how; there is no emotional hook for the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal could fit any organization or funder and lacks tailoring to the specific RFA requirements or demonstration of unique fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to Address Sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: No plan for what happens after the grant ends makes funders worry their investment will be wasted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Describe post-grant plans and a diversification of funding strategy to continue the work beyond the funded period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak Letters of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters that are generic, from inappropriate people, or missing key partners fail to strengthen the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Obtain specific, substantive letters from appropriate partners that address roles, contributions, and organizational commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate Preliminary Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Especially for research grants, lack of preliminary data prevents reviewers from gauging feasibility and makes hypotheses appear untested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Provide appropriate preliminary results or feasibility evidence that supports the proposed approach and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overpromising
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposing more work than can be accomplished within the time/budget demonstrates unrealistic planning and damages credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Align scope with timeline and resources; be realistic about achievable deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underselling
rubrics_metrics.description: Being too modest about innovations or failing to highlight competitive advantages weakens the case for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Clearly state the novelty or advantage of your approach and make a strong case for why funding is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignoring the Funder's Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Not using the funder's preferred language, missing strategic priorities, or failing to show mission alignment undermines fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by: Tailor language and objectives to the RFA/NOFO and demonstrate clear alignment with the funder's strategic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Read RFA/NOFO multiple times
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit checklist item to ensure understanding of requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Verified all required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that every document requested by the funder is prepared and included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Met page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all narrative sections comply with page/word limits set by the funder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Formatted according to guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm font, margins, figure labeling, and other formatting rules match the funder's instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Budget matches narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the budget reflects and is justified by the proposal's goals, timeline, and personnel effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Letters of support obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect all required letters from partners and stakeholders that substantiate commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Biosketches updated
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure CVs/biosketches for key personnel are current and follow funder format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: References complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide complete and correctly formatted references and citations as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Proofread by multiple people
rubrics_metrics.description: Have several reviewers proofread to catch errors and improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Submitted with time to spare
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan submission early to allow for institutional approvals and technical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Submission: Follow-up plan in place
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a plan for post-submission communication and next steps if awarded or declined.
